title: GameCore catalog pack
description: One emulator or application = one directory. seed/, logo.png|logo.svg, generator.py and tests/ are implicit: they are present on disk or they are not, and no field declares them.

emulatorName.description: The product name, when it differs from the platform label: `label` is 'Nintendo 64', this is 'Rosalie's Mupen GUI'. Shown by the graphical installer, which used to carry its own copy of both. Absent = fall back to `label`.

family.description: Who made the hardware: 'Nintendo', 'Sony', 'Microsoft', 'Sega'... The installer groups the catalogue by it, so a box with twenty systems reads as four short lists instead of one long one. Free text on purpose — a pack for a machine nobody here anticipated names its own maker and is grouped with its siblings without a line of UI changing. Absent = grouped under 'Other'; apps are grouped by their kind and ignore this.

description.description: One line shown next to the tick box in the install wizard.

order.description: Where this system sits in the grid, and in the installer's tick list. A curated running order, not alphabetical — the console you reach for most is first. Absent means last, in id order: a pack that forgets it is placed badly, never dropped. Before this field the order was a list of ids inside scripts/gen-catalog.py, and a pack missing from that list was silently absent from both the grid and the installer.

install.description: How the MAIN artifact is obtained. Extra system dependencies go in `packages`, never here.

appIds.description:
Ordered candidates, best first. The installer takes the first one the remote still offers; everything else on the box takes the first one actually installed.

A list and not a string because an upstream can vanish overnight — Ryujinx original left Flathub with no warning, and Ryubing is one maintainer's decision away from the same. With a single id that day broke twice and said neither: the install found nothing, and the tile went on launching a name that no longer existed. A second candidate is the difference between a degraded box and a dead slot.

One entry is perfectly legitimate: it means nobody has found a credible alternative yet, not that the pack forgot.

sandbox.description: Flatpak override. Absent = the emulator policy (filesystem @GAMECORE_PATH@, device all, socket x11). Only meaningful when install.provider is flatpak.

fullscreen.description: For an app with no fullscreen CLI flag (Stremio has none). backend/services/fullscreen_enforcer.py waits for a window whose WM_CLASS matches, then asks the WM to fullscreen it over EWMH.

gamepadTrigger.description: Re-fire udev after launch. A Flatpak app that opens its own window only sees a pad plugged in before it started; this makes one plugged in after it appear. Needs the udevadm sudoers rule.

preferIfPresent.description: Absorbs the REWRITE pass of flatpakify-systems.sh: when this path exists, it wins over the nominal launcher.

bios.description:
The system files the OWNER has to supply, and where they go. Nothing here is ever downloaded, shipped or linked to — this block only says what a working install looks like, so `backend/services/bios.py` can answer 'absent / wrong md5 / conforming' instead of the emulator answering with a black screen.

The information was already in the seeds, unreadable: `catalog/pcsx2/seed/PCSX2.ini` has named `ps2-0150e-20001228.bin` since the first release, and nothing could check whether that file was on the box. A player whose PS2 games all failed to boot got no message naming it.

Declare only what is SOURCED — a filename a seed pins, or one the emulator itself defines. A guessed name produces a permanently red line on a working install, which is the ticket this block exists to remove.

dir.description:
Where the files belong, as a path expression. `@FLATPAK_CONFIG@` and `@FLATPAK_DATA@` expand from the same `install.appIds` entry the box actually has installed — the gopher64 rule — so a BIOS directory under an app id nobody installs is unexpressible. `@HOME@` and `@GAMECORE_PATH@` are also accepted, for the emulators that are not Flatpak.

This is NOT `config.dest`: PCSX2 reads its inis from `PCSX2/inis` and its BIOS from `PCSX2/bios`, Cemu keeps `keys.txt` under data/ and its settings under config/. Deriving one from the other would have named the wrong directory for both.

files.description: The files checked by name. Omit for a system whose emulator scans the directory instead — see `anyFile`.

file.description: Name relative to `dir`, subdirectories allowed. Never absolute and never containing '..': the checker refuses to stat outside `dir`, and a pack that tried would be reading a path the catalogue does not own.

md5.description: Expected fingerprint, when a single dump is the right one. Absent means 'present is all we can check' — a firmware whose hash changes with its version (RPCS3, Ryujinx keys) must NOT carry one, or every legitimate update would be reported as corrupt.

required.description: true = the system does not work without it, and a launch is refused with this filename on screen. false = the install is fine without it (regional firmwares, high-resolution BIOS, keys only some titles need). Red on a working box is the ticket this block was written to stop, so `false` is the answer whenever there is any doubt.

note.description: One line the player reads. What the file is for, never where to get it.

anyFile.description: For an emulator that SCANS `dir` and takes whatever image it recognises — DuckStation's `[BIOS] SearchDirectory`. No filename can be checked because the pack legitimately pins none, so the only honest verdict is 'the directory has something in it' or 'it is empty'. Never carries an md5, for the same reason.

config.description: Where seed/ is deployed. Omit entirely when the pack ships no seed/.

nativeDest.description: Destination when launch.path is not 'flatpak' (mgba, melonds).

order.description: Where this emulator sits in a profiling pass, and therefore in the toast the player sees when a pad is plugged in. Absent means last, in id order. It used to be a tuple of ten ids in backend/services/configgen/__init__.py, and a pack missing from it was never profiled at all — its bindings silently never written.

strategy.description: rewrite-player-block: rpcs3 · rewrite-device-line: dolphin (binds by NAME) · guid-rebind: ryujinx (binds by GUID) · sdl-index-clone: pcsx2/duckstation · snapshot-restore: azahar/mgba/cemu/gopher64 · snapshot-or-synth: melonds · none

multitap.description: The accessory a two-port console needs before slot 3 exists at all. `value` turns it on, `offValue` turns it back off. Both are declared here because a release that had to GUESS the off value would be inventing config, and because the tap belongs to the roster rather than to a slot: nothing switched it off for a long time, so every solo session after one session at four ran with a virtual accessory on port 1.

offValue.description: What the key reads when no player needs the tap — the value the seed ships.

padType.description: The Type= value that keeps sticks and rumble alive (pcsx2 DualShock2, duckstation AnalogController).

seedMustNotContain.description: Python regular expressions (re.M) a seed/ may never match. Regexes, not plain substrings: RPCS3 YAML structurally needs a `Device:` key, and what must be forbidden is a Device that NAMES a controller, not the key itself. A seed that names a device pins the grid to one controller model; CI fails on a hit.

usb.description:
The peripherals this system needs that are NOT SDL gamepads: the GameCube adapter Dolphin drives over raw libusb, a DolphinBar, an arcade stick that enumerates as a keyboard, a wheel, RPCS3's DS3 passthrough.

None of them can enter the roster through `controllers`, and that is the point. `gamepad_monitor` only ever sees a device that declares BTN_SOUTH on an evdev node, so an adapter with no evdev node at all was invisible everywhere: no line on the controllers screen, no udev rule, and no way for the owner to tell 'not plugged in' from 'not supported'.

Declaring one here does four things: it lays the rule down at install (`installer/applier.py`), it lists the device on the controllers screen present-or-absent, it re-fires udev after launch so a device plugged in later reaches the Flatpak sandbox, and it puts the pack's own note on screen when the device is missing.

It never refuses a launch. A USB accessory is optional by nature — Dolphin plays fine with a DualShock 4 — and blocking would be inventing a fault, the mistake `bios.required` exists to avoid.

vidPid.description: Lowercase `vendor:product`, exactly as sysfs writes it in /sys/bus/usb/devices/*/idVendor. Pinned lowercase so a pack and a udev rule that name the same adapter in different case are still the same adapter.

class.description: What KIND of thing it is, which is what the roster was missing. `gamepad` is the case the pipeline already handled; the other four are the ones it could not express. The controllers screen groups by it, and it is the honest answer to 'why does this device not get a player slot' — a light gun never should.

label.description: What the owner calls it — 'GameCube adapter', 'DolphinBar'. Absent = the vidPid is shown, which is correct but unreadable from a sofa.

udevRule.description:
One udev rule line, written to /etc/udev/rules.d/99-gamecore-<pack>.rules at install. Omit when the device needs no rule — plenty work on their kernel defaults, and an unnecessary rule is a permission widened for nothing.

Write the narrowest rule that works: this grants access to a device node, and `MODE="0666"` on a device that also carries a keyboard interface is every keystroke on the box readable by any local uid. The existing 99-gamecore-input.rules documents that trade at length.

note.description: One line the player reads when the device is not detected. What it is for and what to check — the mode switch on a DolphinBar, the USB port a passthrough needs. Never where to buy one.

localMedia.description: The on-disk layout this system's dumps use, so icons, titles and disc serials can be read from the game files themselves instead of guessed from the filename. Absent = this system has no local media and falls back to online scraping, which is exactly what an emulator nobody listed used to get. WHICH parser reads a format is code (backend/services/local_media.py); WHICH format a system uses is this. duckstation and pcsx2 read the identical PlayStation layout and differ by one string — that was six `if sid == …` branches across three functions before it moved here.

format.description: ps3: PS3_GAME/ICON0.PNG + PARAM.SFO · ps4: sce_sys/ · psp: the same two files inside the ISO · gcwii: the 6-char id in the image header · playstation: the serial in SYSTEM.CNF. A new format is new code, so this enum only grows alongside local_media.py.

discTag.description: The kind `disc_id()` returns, when it is not the format name. gcwii reads GameCube and Wii images alike but reports 'wii'; duckstation and pcsx2 share the playstation parser and report 'psx' and 'ps2'. Absent = the format name.

overlay.description: Bezel identification only. window_rect and hole stay in config/overlays.json: they are image/resolution tuning, not a property of the emulator. `label` is NOT repeated here - the pack's own label is used.

packages.description: Extra system dependencies, NOT the main artifact. Aggregated across all selected packs into a single pacman call.

sources.description: git_sync semantics: clone when absent, pull --ff-only otherwise, never over local changes.

ifAbsent.description: Write only when dest does not exist. For a file the owner is expected to hand-edit: re-running the installer is documented as safe, and for the demo EmberTV config that has to mean untouched.

services.description: User units only. arch.sh:668 documents why creating this tree as root broke the kiosk.

postInstall.description: Last resort, bounded: runs as the user, never root, with a timeout, and a failure NEVER interrupts the install - it logs a warning. An ordered list, because some apps need two irreducible steps (generate a cert, then trust it).
